newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Sharp drop seen in Colombian coffee output.
newsitem.headline: Sharp drop seen in Colombian coffee output.

text.p: The head of Colombia's National Exporters' Association, Gabriel Rosas Vega, said he expects the country to produce no more than 10.5 to 11.0 million 60-kg bags of coffee during the current coffee year, down from 12.9 million bags in the 1995-1996 coffee year.

Rosas said production would be adversely affected, at least in part, by what he described as the imminent closure of the heavily indebted National Coffee Fund, which guarantees the purchase of crops from growers and has provided industry-wide stability for decades.
The fund has been hard hit by the recent strengthening of Colombia's peso, which erodes the value of export revenues, and Rosas said it could be forced to shut down within three months.
Speaking at a news conference, he said cash-strapped growers had been sent reeling by soaring production costs and were in no position to boost output through capital spending.
Rosas also said bad weather in the central coffee-growing region of Quindio and Risaralda could reduce output but he did not elaborate.
